First, recall that:

$$
{lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)=({lim}_{t\to 2}{t}^{2})\,i+({lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{t-4}{2})\,j+({lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{1}{t})\,k
$$

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

- For the first component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}{t}^{2} & ={2}^{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{t-4}{2} & =\frac{2-4}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2}{2} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{1}{t} & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)=4\,i-j+\frac{1}{2}\,k.$
